says: Taking all three. The wall is rebuilt from scratch: strata bands now run along the path and are split into fractured slabs, each facet hatched at its own angle and density, about a third left white as lit faces, with dark shadow under the ledge lips and a few deep cracks. The strider is bigger and is now the clearest shape on the page: closed, tapering legs with forward knees, backward ankles and splayed clawed toes, the far leg nearly solid; saddle with a high cantle, striped cloth, girth and breast straps, bridle and reins; the cloak trails behind. The stone head now has the far strata and cracks running through it, a chipped nose, and stipple instead of hatching.
